# dsh-plugin-update-checker
> English · 中文
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that adds a **Check updates** button to the **Built-in plugins** settings
section. Click it and the plugin scans every installed plugin bundle for (1) the latest published ve
rsion on the npm registry and (2) its compatibility with the running DSH runtime — then shows one ro
npm registry and (2) its compatibility with the running DSH runtime — then shows one row per bundle.
It lives beside the read-only inventory tab and contributes **no configuration** of its own. It repo
rts, and for any bundle with a published update it offers a single **Update** button. Enabling, disa
bling, or removing a bundle is still done in the sidebar **Plugins** page or via `dsh plugin`.
**How the Update button works**: the host drives the app's own plugin manager, and an update is two
manager calls — `removeBundle`, then `installBundle(<name>@<version>)`. One call is not enough: dsh
0.2.1's manager refuses `add` for a package that is already a profile dependency (`already-installed
`, thrown before pnpm runs), which is exactly the shape of an update. The installed version is read
back off disk afterwards, so a manager that reports success without writing anything surfaces as a f
ailure instead of a version bump. One bundle is deliberately excluded: this plugin cannot remove its
elf, because removing it would unload the route serving the request — update it with `dsh install-pl
ugin dsh-plugin-update-checker@<version>` instead.
## ✨ What it does
| Check | Source | Notes |
| **Update availability** | npm registry (`latest` dist-tag vs the installed version) | Registry-onl
y. Bundles installed from a tarball / git / path publish nothing, so they are reported as *Unsupport

ed* rather than falsely *Up to date*. |
| **Compatibility** | the bundle's `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` `peer
Dependencies` vs the running DSH version | Reuses `@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot`'s `evaluatePluginCompa
tibility`, the same helper the launcher applies on boot. An exact-version exemption granted in `comp
atibility.json` shows as *Compatible (exempted)*. |
Compatibility and update availability are computed **independently** — a slow or unreachable registr
y can never hide an incompatible peer range, and a local-only bundle still gets a compatibility verd
n never hide an incompatible peer range, and a local-only bundle still gets a compatibility verdict.
**Which registry the scan asks**: no longer a hardcoded `registry.npmjs.org`. The host reads the con
figuration itself (environment → the profile's `.npmrc` → the user's `~/.npmrc`, first hit wins) and
then **probes the candidates concurrently, taking the first success**. Three cases: **nothing confi
gured** → race the launcher's mirror against the public registry; **the public default configured**
(npm writes `registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/` into `~/.npmrc` on its own) → keep it and add the
mirror behind it, since both are public and nothing leaks; **anything else configured** (a corporat
e or internal registry) → **that one alone, never raced against a public registry**, because racing
would leak internal package names to third parties. The difference is large behind a slow link — mea
sured on one machine, the public registry answered in ~11 s where a mirror answered in ~0.2 s, and r
acing means a slow registry cannot hold up a fast one even when it is listed first. A bundle that de
clares `publishConfig.registry` still uses that registry. The winning registry travels with the row
and is reused by the one-click update, so **the version is read from, and installed from, the same p
reused by the one-click update, so **the version is read from, and installed from, the same p [长行截断]

## 📸 Where it sits
Open **Settings → Built-in plugins**. The section now has two tabs:

- **Plugin list** — the read-only inventory (shipped by DSH).
- **Check updates** — this plugin. It
shows the running DSH version, a **Check updates** button, and the results table (plugin / installed
/ latest / compatibility / update).
The check is on demand: click the button, the host scans, and the table fills in. One broken manifes
t or an unreachable registry is isolated to its own row — it never blanks the whole report.

## 📝 Limitations
- **Reports and updates, does not toggle** — it never enables, disables, or removes a bundle on its
own initiative; the removal in an update is the manager's own two-step for that one bundle. A failed

update is reported per row, not retried automatically.
- **Cannot update itself** — the Update butt
on is replaced by a clear refusal; use `dsh install-plugin dsh-plugin-update-checker@<version>` from

a terminal, then restart.
- **Reports the runtime, never updates it** — the DSH runtime row has no
Update button in any carrier. On the desktop it reads **Updated by the app** and points at the menu
bar; on a CLI/web host it keeps *Update available* and shows the `npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@<v
ersion>` command. Naming the actor is deliberate: a button this panel cannot honour reads as a broke

n control.
- **Registry reachability** — registry checks need network access to the configured regis

try; offline or firewalled hosts show *Unknown* per bundle.
- **Local / git / tarball bundles** — pu
blish no registry version, so their update status is *Unsupported*. Their compatibility is still eva
luated from the local manifest.
